title: BRC poised to take first innings points
Dulani leads Sri Lanka to victory with maiden international ton | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 1 August 2026 03:44
-     - 4

Muneeba Ali smashed a 24-ball 42

Imesha Dulani and Chamari Athapaththu added 78 runs for the first wicket

First Women’s T20I v Pakistan at Dambulla

Imesha Dulani led 

Sri Lanka’s charge with a maiden unbeaten century

Shawaal Zulifiqar top scored for Pakistan with 63

Imesha Dulani, widely regarded as one of the most promising batters in the Sri Lanka women’s cricket team hit a spectacular unbeaten maiden WT20I century to guide her team to a comprehensive six wickets win against Pakistan in the first Women’s T20 International played at the Rangiri Dambulla Cricket Stadium yesterday.

Opening the batting with her legendary skipper Chamari Athapaththu, Player of the Match Dulani smashed 17 fours and one six in her knock of 101* as Sri Lanka chased down Pakistan’s total of 176-7 to win with an over to spare.

Dulani became only the second Sri Lankan woman to score a T20I hundred after Athapaththu (39 off 22 balls, 5 fours, 2 sixes) with whom she shared an opening stand of 78 off 43 balls.

Dulani held her end up despite the cheap dismissals of Vishmi Gunaratne and Harshitha Samarawickrama to forge a 52 runs stand off 36 balls with Kavisha Dilhari (11) to bring Sri Lanka within 10 runs of victory.

Pakistan were left to feel that they had let the match slip out of their fingers after dominating the batting powerplay by posting 64-0 in the first six overs. Muneeba Ali contributed 41 of those runs off 22 balls, but soon after the powerplay ended she lost her wicket for 42 off 24 balls (9 fours). 

However, her opening partner Shawaal Zulfiqar took control from there onwards scoring 63 off 41 balls (10 fours, 1 six) and with small contributions from the middle and late order Pakistan managed to come up with a challenging total of 176-7. 

Pakistan will be pleased with their top order batting, but having gone into the final five overs at 127-2, they might have hoped for more in their last five than the 49 they got.  

It was the spinners who bowled well on the wicket with Kaveesha Dilhari claiming 2/36 for Sri Lanka and left-arm spinner Nashra Sandhu 2/25 for Pakistan. The second WT20I will be played on Sunday at the same venue. – [ST]

Scores: 

Pakistan Women 176-7 (20) (Muneeba Ali 42, Shawaal Zulfiqar 63, Eman Naseer 21, Kavisha Dilhari 2.36) vs. Sri Lanka Women 177-4 (19) (Imesha Dulani 101*, Chamari Athapaththu 39, Nashra Sandhu 2/25)

title: Asia Pacific Lions vs. Northampton Saints on 28 Aug. | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 1 August 2026 03:33
-     - 5

Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Sunil Kumara Gamage (second from right) receiving the sponsorship cheque. Others (from left): Project Chairman Rohan Abeykoon, DASA Group UK CEO Nakeeb Atheek, Inthi Marikar, and Asia Pacific Lions Founder and Director Saabir Cader

By Shamseer Jaleel

The Asia Pacific Lions vs. Northampton Saints Tour of Sri Lanka 2026, a landmark initiative set to elevate Sri Lanka’s status on the international rugby stage, is backed by DASA Group UK as the Title Sponsor.

The highlight of the tour will be the historic clash between English Premiership champions Northampton Saints and the newly formed Asia Pacific Lions, an invitational team featuring leading players from Asia Rugby member unions and the Pacific Islands.

The match will kick off on 28 August at the Racecourse International Stadium in Colombo, promising Sri Lankan rugby fans a rare opportunity to witness some of the world’s top players in action.

Beyond the feature match, the tour will include rugby coaching clinics, youth development programs, community outreach, tourism promotions, corporate engagements, media activities, and a charity T20 cricket match involving rugby stars and Sri Lankan cricket legends.

Organisers believe these initiatives will create a lasting legacy by developing local rugby while promoting Sri Lanka as a premier destination for international sporting events.

The Youth Affairs and Sports Ministry, Sri Lanka Tourism, DASA Group UK, Pearl Isle Capital, City of Dreams Sri Lanka, Aitken Spence Travels, ThePapare, Asiri Health, and TRU will also support the tour.

title: AFC backs UEFA and CONCACAF who plan boycott over FIFA World Cup proposals | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 1 August 2026 03:31
-     - 6

Asia Football Confederation President Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa (centre) has joined the criticism of the plans by FIFA President Gianni Infantino

The ‌Asian Football Confederation has said it “stands in solidarity” with regional bodies UEFA and CONCACAF in opposing plans to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors but stopped short of threatening ⁠to boycott events run by FIFA, global football’s governing body.

The confederation in a statement on Friday expressed “deep concern” over the proposed establishment of a $20bn commercial ⁠subsidiary, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), to run the World Cup and FIFA’s other events.

“The fact that the situation has reached the point where the real possibility of a FIFA World Cup boycott has entered public discourse should concern everyone ‌who cares about the future of our game,” the statement said.

“Football should never have been placed in such a position.”

UEFA, European football’s governing body, voted unanimously on Thursday to boycott all FIFA events unless the plans were dropped. CONCACAF, the regional federation for North America, Central America and the Caribbean, has also rejected FIFA’s proposal.

On Thursday, AFC President Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim Al Khalifa had said the way the proposal had been made was “totally unacceptable”, in a letter to member associations.

The AFC said “the proposed FFE cannot realistically achieve the necessary broad consensus and unity required to move forward.

“The FIFA World Cup is the pinnacle of global football and derives its strength from the participation of all confederations and the world’s leading football nations.”

The AFC also made a thinly veiled attack on the governing body’s president, Gianni Infantino, saying the plan “has exposed fundamental weaknesses in FIFA’s consultation and decision-making processes that must now be addressed”.

Even after FIFA issued ⁠a new statement on Friday, saying each national association “should be allowed to review the proposal and have a say in shaping their own future”, the AFC said “central concerns surrounding governance, ‌institutional process and meaningful consultation remain unanswered”.
